device.name: Two-Spool High-Bypass Turbofan Engine
device.summary: A representative large turbofan in which a wide fan produces most thrust while a compact gas-generator core compresses air, burns fuel, and drives two concentric turbine-and-shaft systems.
device.disclaimer: Representative internals of this kind of device, not an exact copy of one product. Stage counts, dimensions, accessory locations, and internal geometry are simplified for study.

parts.name: Nacelle Inlet Lip
parts.function: The rounded leading edge accelerates incoming air smoothly into the fan while resisting icing and bird impacts.
parts.howItWorks: Its continuous curved surface lets the flow turn into the inlet without a sharp separation point. Hot compressor bleed air can warm internal passages near the lip during icing conditions. The deep rounded profile also tolerates airflow arriving at an angle during takeoff and crosswind operation.
parts.engineering: The lip is shaped for a broad incidence range rather than one ideal streamline. Anti-ice performance is limited by available bleed heat and by the thermal resistance of the skin; local stresses also include bird strike and pressure pulsations from the fan.
parts.material: Formed aluminium alloy with erosion-resistant leading-edge treatment
failureModes: Bird-strike denting and delamination of bonded panels

parts.name: Fan Cowl
parts.function: This removable outer nacelle barrel streamlines the engine and provides access to the fan case and accessories.
parts.howItWorks: The cowl carries aerodynamic loads around the fan module while leaving a separate structural containment case underneath. Split lines, hinges, and latches allow maintenance crews to open it without removing the engine. Its inner surface also helps define the forward bypass passage.
parts.engineering: The cowl must be light and stiff but is not normally the primary blade-containment structure. Latch preload and panel stiffness control flutter and gap steps; a small external discontinuity can create measurable drag at cruise speed.
parts.material: Carbon-fibre composite sandwich panels with aluminium frames

parts.name: Aft Nacelle and Bypass Duct Outer Wall
parts.function: The aft nacelle surrounds the bypass stream and shields the core and services behind the fan cowl.
parts.howItWorks: Its inner wall guides fan air rearward around the core with gradually changing area. Its outer wall forms part of the aircraft's external aerodynamic surface. Access panels and attachments accommodate ducts, wiring, and the accessory installation.
parts.engineering: The duct contour trades wetted area and nacelle diameter against bypass pressure recovery. Acoustic treatment and tight panel joints reduce noise, while thermal insulation protects composite structure near the hot core.
parts.material: Composite sandwich skin with metallic frames and heat shielding

parts.name: Bypass Outlet Nozzle
parts.function: The converging aft opening turns bypass pressure into a rearward jet and sets the fan stream's effective back pressure.
parts.howItWorks: Bypass air accelerates through the decreasing exit area. At ordinary subsonic operating points the jet is normally unchoked, so its velocity depends on fan pressure ratio and losses around the duct. The nozzle and core plug together influence mixing behind the engine.
parts.engineering: For an ideal unchoked nozzle, V approximately equals sqrt(2 cp T0 times the quantity 1 minus (p exit / p0) raised to ((gamma minus 1)/gamma)). Real performance is reduced by friction, flow angularity, and pressure thrust mismatch.
parts.material: Titanium and aluminium alloy structure with acoustic treatment

parts.name: Inlet Acoustic Liner
parts.function: The perforated inner barrel absorbs sound generated by the fan before it radiates forward.
parts.howItWorks: Small openings connect the duct to honeycomb cavities behind the visible face sheet. Air motion in the holes dissipates acoustic energy, while cavity depth tunes attenuation toward selected fan tones. Several axial bands provide broader frequency coverage than one cavity depth.
parts.engineering: A quarter-wave cavity has a characteristic depth near wavelength divided by four, although grazing flow and perforated-face resistance shift the optimum. Treatment area, structural weight, contamination, and boundary-layer thickness limit the achievable attenuation.
parts.material: Perforated aluminium face sheet bonded to aluminium honeycomb

parts.name: Fan Containment Case
parts.function: This structural ring carries fan-case loads and is designed to contain fragments from a released fan blade.
parts.howItWorks: A hard inner ring resists initial cutting while a tough outer wrap absorbs energy and catches debris. The case also supports the fan exit structure and maintains the tip-clearance environment during normal operation. It is intentionally much heavier than the aerodynamic cowl outside it.
parts.engineering: Blade-off containment is an extreme dynamic event involving local penetration, large ring deformation, and unbalanced rotor loads. Tip clearance must remain small for efficiency, yet the case must tolerate rubs without turning a minor contact into a structural failure.
parts.material: Aluminium or steel inner case with layered aramid-fibre containment wrap

parts.name: Fan Spinner
parts.function: The spinner fairs the fan hub into the incoming flow and helps protect the hub region from ice accumulation.
parts.howItWorks: Its pointed surface divides incoming air between the core inlet and the outer fan passage. Rotation discourages some ice accretion, while its shape prevents a large separated wake immediately ahead of the blade roots. The rear flange attaches to the rotating fan assembly.
parts.engineering: The spinner sees centrifugal loads, bird impact, hail, and cyclic attachment stresses. A smooth external shape must coexist with a stiff,inspectable rear joint and adequate clearance to stationary inlet structure.
parts.material: Aluminium alloy or titanium shell with an elastomeric erosion-resistant nose

parts.name: Wide-Chord Fan Blades
parts.function: The fan blades add energy to a very large airflow, producing most of the engine's thrust and feeding air to the core.
parts.howItWorks: Each swept, twisted blade behaves like a rotating wing. Its aerodynamic section creates a pressure rise while throwing air rearward, and the inner portion supplies the core while the much larger outer portion feeds the bypass duct. The wide chord provides stiffness and resistance to foreign-object damage.
parts.engineering: Fan work follows Euler turbomachinery form delta h0 = U times delta V theta. Relative flow near the tips can be supersonic, so sweep controls shock losses. Wide-chord blades reduce count and weight but demand careful control of flutter, bird-strike response, and root stress.
parts.material: Hollow titanium wide-chord blades with metallic leading-edge protection

parts.name: Fan Disk
parts.function: The disk retains every fan blade and transfers their torque into the low-pressure shaft.
parts.howItWorks: Blade roots sit in shaped slots around the rim, converting enormous centrifugal loads into disk hoop stress. The central bore and flange connect the fan to its shaft and bearing system. Retention features prevent forward or rearward blade movement.
parts.engineering: Disk rim speed dominates stress: centrifugal loading scales with density times omega squared times radius squared. Slot geometry trades local stress concentration against ease of blade replacement, and the disk is commonly treated as a life-limited part.
parts.material: High-strength titanium alloy forging
failureModes: Disk burst following an undetected crack

parts.name: Forward Fan Bearing
parts.function: The forward bearing supports the fan shaft radially while allowing it to rotate with very low friction.
parts.howItWorks: Rolling elements separate the rotating inner race from the stationary outer race. Oil jets lubricate and cool the contact surfaces, and seals retain oil inside the bearing chamber. Other bearings in the engine carry the principal axial thrust.
parts.engineering: Bearing chamber design combines oil delivery, sealing air, heat removal, and tolerance for rotor whirl. Rolling-element speed, often expressed by a bore-and-speed parameter, affects lubrication and cage stability.
parts.material: Hardened bearing steel races and rollers with a high-temperature cage

parts.name: Low-Pressure Shaft
parts.function: The inner shaft transmits power from the rear low-pressure turbine to the front fan and booster.
parts.howItWorks: It runs through the hollow high-pressure shaft so the two spools can turn at different speeds. Long, slender geometry keeps the central gas-path bore small, but requires carefully placed bearings and balancing. Splines and flanges route torque into the fan and turbine disks.
parts.engineering: A multi-metre shaft must avoid critical-speed and whirl problems over its full operating range. Torsional stress is approximately tau = T r / J, while concentric-running clearance and differential thermal growth complicate support design.
parts.material: High-strength nickel or steel alloy shaft with precision-ground journals

parts.name: Fan Outlet Guide Vanes
parts.function: The stationary vanes remove swirl from fan air and straighten the bypass flow.
parts.howItWorks: Fan blades leave the air rotating around the engine axis as well as moving rearward. These cambered vanes turn that tangential motion back toward the axial direction, recovering useful pressure and reducing downstream losses. They also form structural connections across the bypass annulus.
parts.engineering: The vanes trade swirl recovery against their own profile drag and wake loss. Their spacing and sweep influence fan-tone propagation, and structural versions must carry case loads without excessively disturbing the flow.
parts.material: Titanium or aluminium alloy vanes with composite or metallic ducts

parts.name: Intermediate Case
parts.function: This structural frame joins the core to the fan case and carries services across the bypass duct.
parts.howItWorks: A small number of thick radial struts transmit mount and bearing loads while exposing most of the annulus to airflow. The lower region provides a route for the accessory drive. Its inner ring supports core structure and its outer ring joins the fan containment structure.
parts.engineering: Struts must be thinner than a solid web for low blockage yet strong enough for imbalance and blade-off loads. Fuel, oil, electrical, and mechanical drive paths crossing the annulus need aerodynamic fairings and thermal protection.
parts.material: Cast or fabricated titanium alloy with steel service fittings
failureModes: Service-line chafing inside the strut fairings

parts.name: Low-Pressure Compressor Rotors
parts.function: Three booster stages begin compressing core air before it enters the high-pressure compressor.
parts.howItWorks: Each rotating row adds swirl and total pressure, and the following stationary row converts part of that velocity into static pressure. The stages are mounted on the low-pressure spool, so their speed is tied to the fan. Their flow areas decrease as the air becomes denser.
parts.engineering: A stage cannot simply add unlimited work: excessive turning or diffusion promotes boundary-layer separation. Blade stagger and radius are chosen to keep relative Mach number, diffusion, and hub and tip stresses within workable limits.
parts.material: Titanium alloy disks and blades

parts.name: Booster Stator Vanes
parts.function: Stationary vane rows redirect and diffuse the flow between booster rotor stages.
parts.howItWorks: Each row removes some of the swirl created by the preceding rotor. Diffusion slows the relative flow and raises static pressure before the next rotor receives it. Outer shrouds locate the vane ends and maintain the annulus shape.
parts.engineering: Stator incidence varies with spool speed and throttle setting. Excess positive incidence can stall a vane row, while large clearances permit leakage that wastes the work added by the rotor.
parts.material: Titanium alloy vanes and steel shroud rings

parts.name: High-Pressure Spool Thrust Bearing
parts.function: This bearing locates the high-pressure rotor and carries its large axial aerodynamic load.
parts.howItWorks: Angular-contact rolling elements support both radial motion and thrust along the shaft axis. A squeeze-film or similar mounting arrangement can help control vibration. Pressurised bearing seals keep lubricating oil away from the compressor flow path.
parts.engineering: The net rotor thrust comes from pressure acting on many disk and blade surfaces and changes strongly with power setting. Bearing sizing must include transient load reversals as well as steady thrust, oil-jet cooling, and thermal expansion of the support.
parts.material: Through-hardened or case-hardened bearing steel

parts.name: Variable Compressor Inlet Guide Vanes
parts.function: Adjustable inlet vanes set the airflow angle entering the high-pressure compressor.
parts.howItWorks: At low spool speed the vanes close to reduce incidence on the first rotor and improve stall margin. They open as speed and airflow rise. An external ring and linkage move the row together under commands from the electronic control.
parts.engineering: Variable geometry schedules are coordinated with bleed valves during starting and rapid transients. Actuator backlash, vane bushing friction, and thermal distortion can create stagger errors large enough to reduce compressor stability margin.
parts.material: Titanium vanes with steel pivot hardware and actuation rings

specs.label: Typical motion
specs.value: Several tens of degrees of stagger change

parts.name: High-Pressure Compressor Rotor Stack
parts.function: Six represented rotor stages raise core-air pressure to the level required for efficient combustion.
parts.howItWorks: The stacked disks rotate on the high-pressure shaft and add work in successive steps. Blade height falls toward the rear because compressed air occupies less volume. Clamped or bolted drum features transmit torque while preserving concentricity at high speed.
parts.engineering: Rear stages run hot enough that material choice can change from titanium toward higher-temperature alloys. Blade tips operate with very small clearances; a few tenths of a millimetre of leakage can materially reduce stage efficiency, but centrifugal and case thermal growth vary through each transient.
parts.material: Titanium front stages and higher-temperature nickel or steel alloy rear stages

specs.label: Representative modern overall pressure ratio class

parts.name: High-Pressure Compressor Stators
parts.function: Stationary rows diffuse and reorient the air between high-pressure rotor stages.
parts.howItWorks: The cambered vanes recover static pressure from rotor-generated swirl and deliver air at an angle the next rotor can accept. Outer rings support the vane ends and form part of the compressor flow-path boundary. Some rows in a real engine may also have adjustable stagger.
parts.engineering: A multistage compressor is highly sensitive to matching: one stage operating far from its design incidence changes conditions for all downstream rows. Vane wakes, end-wall leakage, and surface roughness accumulate into overall efficiency loss.
parts.material: Titanium or corrosion-resistant steel vanes with alloy shrouds

parts.name: Hollow High-Pressure Shaft
parts.function: The outer concentric shaft connects the high-pressure turbine to the high-pressure compressor.
parts.howItWorks: It surrounds the low-pressure shaft without being mechanically locked to it. The high-pressure turbine supplies just enough power to drive its compressor and associated losses. A hollow section saves weight and leaves room for the inner shaft and bearing system.
parts.engineering: The two-spool arrangement lets each compressor operate nearer its preferred speed over the thrust range. Shaft wall thickness must manage torque projects, burst containment implications, critical speeds, and bore clearance during unequal thermal expansion.
parts.material: High-strength nickel or steel alloy forging

specs.label: Construction
specs.value: Hollow shaft surrounding the low-pressure spool

parts.name: Compressor Case
parts.function: The split pressure case supports compressor stators and maintains the blade-tip flow-path boundary.
parts.howItWorks: Its inner contour follows the shrinking compressor annulus while its outer shell carries pressure and structural loads. Flanges and bore bosses provide access for variable vanes, bleed ports, and sensors. Active clearance control in some engines pipes air around similar cases to change their temperature.
parts.engineering: Case ovality can be as important as its mean diameter because the closest blade tip determines rub risk. Thick flanges improve stiffness but add weight and slow thermal response, increasing transient clearance mismatch.
parts.material: Titanium or nickel-alloy forward case sections with steel flanges

parts.name: Compressor Exit Diffuser
parts.function: The diffuser slows the last compressor stage's fast discharge before air enters the combustor.
parts.howItWorks: Expanding passages convert velocity into static pressure and distribute the air more evenly around the annulus. Lower velocity reduces combustor pressure loss and makes a stable flame easier to maintain. Radial passages and structural vanes help guide the strongly swirling discharge.
parts.engineering: Aggressive diffusion shortens the engine but risks flow separation and total-pressure loss. The design must deliver circumferentially uniform conditions despite upstream blade wakes and changes in compressor operating point.
parts.material: Nickel-based high-temperature alloy

parts.name: Compressor Bleed Valves
parts.function: Opening these ports unloads selected compressor stages during starting and rapid transients.
parts.howItWorks: The electronic controller commands valves to release some interstage air into a duct or bypass region. This changes stage matching and increases margin against compressor surge. The valves close at higher power so the engine does not waste compressed air unnecessarily.
parts.engineering: Bleed flow is a direct efficiency penalty but a valuable stability tool. Valve timing is tightly coordinated with acceleration fuel schedules and variable vanes; leaks or slow actuation can cause either poor performance or insufficient surge margin.
parts.material: Stainless steel valves with high-temperature seals and actuators

parts.name: Combustor Outer Case
parts.function: The pressure case contains compressor discharge pressure and supports the combustor liner and fuel system.
parts.howItWorks: Air inside the case surrounds the liner before entering through its dome and wall openings. The pressure difference helps distribute cooling and combustion air through the liner. Ports support fuel nozzles, igniters, instrumentation, and borescope inspection.
parts.engineering: The case is primarily a pressure vessel but also sees local thermal gradients and nozzle-mount loads. Opening layout must preserve hoop strength while permitting inspection and replacement of hot-section hardware.
parts.material: Nickel-based high-temperature alloy

parts.name: Annular Combustor Liner
parts.function: The liner provides a protected annular space in which fuel mixes with air and burns continuously.
parts.howItWorks: Swirlers and dome openings create a recirculation zone that anchors the flame. Additional holes admit air for mixing and wall cooling, then dilution air shapes the temperature profile entering the turbine. The liner confines hot gas but is itself protected by cooler air films and thermal barrier coatings.
parts.engineering: Combustion must remain stable from idle to takeoff while limiting smoke, nitrogen oxides, and pressure loss. Liner life often depends more on local metal temperature and cyclic gradients than on the bulk gas temperature.
parts.material: Nickel-based superalloy sheet with thermal barrier coating

parts.name: Annular Fuel Manifold
parts.function: The manifold distributes metered fuel around all combustor nozzles.
parts.howItWorks: A ring-shaped passage feeds many branches so every nozzle sees nearly the same supply pressure. Its rigid support holds the nozzles in alignment while accommodating thermal expansion. Valve scheduling may split flow between nozzle circuits at different power settings.
parts.engineering: Unequal branch restriction creates circumferential fuel-flow variation and a distorted turbine inlet temperature profile. The manifold also needs drainage, purging, and resistance to vibration and fuel coking at nearby hot surfaces.
parts.material: Stainless steel tubing with welded high-temperature fittings

parts.name: Fuel Nozzles and Air Swirlers
parts.function: The nozzles atomise and distribute fuel while surrounding swirlers establish the combustor's mixing pattern.
parts.howItWorks: Fuel leaves each nozzle as a fine spray rather than a solid stream. High-velocity swirling air breaks the spray into droplets, entrains it, and forms a recirculating flame-stabilisation region. Uniform nozzle behaviour helps avoid hot sectors in the turbine.
parts.engineering: Droplet size depends on fuel properties, pressure differential, air momentum, and nozzle geometry. Very small passages promote fine atomisation but are vulnerable to contamination and coke deposits near hot walls.
parts.material: Stainless steel and nickel alloy with precision-machined metering passages

parts.name: Combustor Igniters
parts.function: Two high-energy igniters establish the initial flame during starting and provide relight capability when commanded.
parts.howItWorks: Each igniter produces an intense spark near a fuel-rich part of the combustor dome. Once the flame spreads around the annulus and becomes self-sustaining, continuous ignition is normally unnecessary. Dual igniters improve reliability without requiring one at every nozzle.
parts.engineering: Relight depends on local pressure, temperature, fuel vaporisation, and airspeed, especially at high altitude or after a flameout. Igniter tips survive severe thermal cycling and require a compromise between spark exposure and erosion protection.
parts.material: Nickel alloy body with ceramic insulation and high-temperature electrode

parts.name: High-Pressure Turbine Nozzle Guide Vanes
parts.function: These stationary hot-section vanes accelerate combustion gas and direct it onto the high-pressure turbine blades.
parts.howItWorks: Converging passages turn pressure energy into high velocity and set the flow angle at the rotor inlet. Cooling air passes through internal vane passages and may leave through small surface holes. The row experiences some of the most severe gas temperatures in the engine.
parts.engineering: The first turbine nozzle strongly influences stage work and heat transfer. Cooling uses valuable compressor air, so designers trade vane life against cycle efficiency and must control film-hole blockage, oxidation, and thermally induced stress.
parts.material: Cast nickel-based superalloy with internal cooling passages and ceramic coating

parts.name: High-Pressure Turbine Disk and Blades
parts.function: The high-pressure turbine extracts enough gas energy to drive the high-pressure compressor.
parts.howItWorks: Hot gas turns through the rotor blade passages and gives up work, torque, and pressure. The disk transfers that torque into the high-pressure shaft. Blade internal passages and external cooling films protect the metal from gas that can be hotter than the alloy's ordinary melting range.
parts.engineering: Turbine power is P = mass flow times cp times total-temperature drop. Single-crystal blades, oxidation-resistant coatings, and internal cooling improve capability, but centrifugal stress still scales with omega squared and makes disk and blade attachment life critical.
parts.material: Nickel-based superalloy disk with cooled single-crystal turbine blades

specs.label: Representative power role
specs.value: Drives only the high-pressure spool and associated losses

parts.name: Turbine Blade Shroud and Seals
parts.function: The stationary shroud forms the outer gas-path wall just above the high-pressure turbine blade tips.
parts.howItWorks: A small tip gap limits gas from leaking over the blades without doing useful work. Segmented rings and knife-edge or honeycomb seals accommodate thermal movement while tolerating occasional contact. Cooling prevents the shroud from distorting excessively.
parts.engineering: Tip leakage loss rises rapidly as clearance grows, but insufficient cold clearance can cause a destructive rub during acceleration. Segment supports must manage roundness, oxidation, and different thermal time constants between disk and case.
parts.material: Nickel-alloy shroud segments with abradable honeycomb seals and ceramic coating

parts.name: Low-Pressure Turbine Stators
parts.function: These vane rows prepare the expanding gas for each low-pressure turbine rotor.
parts.howItWorks: The flow continues expanding through successively larger annuli. Each stator accelerates and turns the gas so the following rotor can extract tangential work efficiently. Larger radius and blade height compensate for falling gas density.
parts.engineering: Rear turbine stages run cooler than the first high-pressure stage but contain much longer blades and more flow area. End-wall losses and exit swirl become increasingly important because the fan demands substantial turbine power.
parts.material: Nickel-based cast or wrought superalloy

parts.name: Low-Pressure Turbine Rotor Stack
parts.function: Four represented turbine stages extract the power needed to drive the fan and booster.
parts.howItWorks: Each expanding rotor row converts gas energy into shaft torque. The disks are joined into the rear end of the low-pressure shaft, whose rotation is independent of the high-pressure spool. The increasing diameter preserves blade speed and flow area as pressure falls.
parts.engineering: Fan power is large, so the low-pressure turbine generally has more stages than the high-pressure turbine. Long rear blades face centrifugal stress, untwist, vibration modes, and aerodynamic duty changes between takeoff and cruise.
parts.material: Nickel-based superalloy blades and high-strength alloy disks

specs.label: Output
specs.value: Mechanical power to the fan and booster

parts.name: Rear Low-Pressure Shaft Bearing
parts.function: The rear bearing supports the low-pressure rotor near the turbine and bearing-sump structure.
parts.howItWorks: Rolling elements carry radial rotor loads while oil lubrication and sealing air protect the chamber. The support includes flexible structural paths for thermal expansion between the shaft and turbine frame. It helps maintain shaft alignment at the turbine disks.
parts.engineering: This location combines high temperature, rotor flexibility, and limited space for cooling and scavenging. Oil leakage into the hot gas path can create smoke or fire risk, while inadequate scavenging can churn and overheat the lubricant.
parts.material: High-temperature bearing steel with alloy support housing

parts.name: Turbine Case
parts.function: The turbine case supports nozzle and shroud hardware and controls the outer hot-gas-path clearance.
parts.howItWorks: Its expanding inner contour follows the low-pressure turbine annulus. Cooling or clearance-control air can condition the case so it expands in a controlled way relative to the rotor. External flanges join the combustor and rear exhaust structures.
parts.engineering: Heavy cases resist distortion but respond slowly to throttle changes, producing transient clearance peaks. Segmented shrouds and controlled cooling seek efficient cruise clearances without takeoff or shutdown rubs.
parts.material: Nickel-based high-temperature alloy with cooled support rings

parts.name: Turbine Exit Frame
parts.function: The rear frame supports the aft bearing and straightens residual swirl before the core exhaust nozzle.
parts.howItWorks: Aerodynamic struts connect the central bearing housing to the outer exhaust ring. They carry structural loads while turning the turbine discharge toward the axial direction. Internal passages route oil and cooling services through the hot exhaust region.
parts.engineering: The struts trade pressure recovery and low blockage against bearing-support stiffness. Thermal gradients can shift bearing alignment, so the frame must remain both strong and predictably flexible.
parts.material: Nickel-based alloy struts and rings with thermal shielding

parts.name: Core Exhaust Cone
parts.function: The central cone fairs the rear bearing region and guides core gas into the exhaust jet.
parts.howItWorks: Its tapered surface prevents a large separated wake behind the central hub. It also shields rear hardware from direct hot-gas recirculation. The surrounding annular flow exits between this cone and the core nozzle wall.
parts.engineering: Cone angle balances pressure recovery against separation and length. Thermal protection is needed because radiation and recirculating hot gas can overheat the enclosed support and service lines.
parts.material: Nickel-based sheet alloy with internal heat shielding

parts.name: Core Exhaust Nozzle
parts.function: The annular core nozzle accelerates remaining turbine discharge into a rearward jet.
parts.howItWorks: After most useful turbine work has been extracted, residual pressure and heat still produce exhaust thrust. The nozzle controls core back pressure and discharges the jet close to the much larger bypass stream. Mixing between the streams influences thrust and noise.
parts.engineering: The nozzle operates at lower pressure ratio than the turbine nozzles but must preserve area and alignment under thermal load. Core and bypass jet mixing can recover some performance, although excessive mixer losses or base drag offset the benefit.
parts.material: Nickel-based high-temperature alloy

parts.name: Accessory Gearbox
parts.function: The gearbox takes mechanical power from a high-pressure rotor drive and powers engine accessories.
parts.howItWorks: A radial drive and internal gear train turn the starter, fuel pump, oil pump, and other accessories at suitable speeds. During starting the torque path reverses so the starter cranks the high-pressure spool. The housing supports bearings, oil jets, and accessory mounting pads.
parts.engineering: Gear tooth loads, accessory torque, and starting transients set shaftarg and casing stiffness. Extracting accessory power reduces net engine output, so efficient gearing and suitably sized pumps matter even though their power is small beside the main turbomachinery.
parts.material: Cast aluminium or magnesium housing with hardened steel gears

parts.name: Engine Starter
parts.function: The starter rotates the high-pressure spool until compressor airflow and combustion can sustain acceleration.
parts.howItWorks: A pneumatic or electrical machine delivers torque through the accessory gearbox. As the spool accelerates, the igniters and fuel system establish combustion. The starter disengages when turbine power exceeds the required acceleration and compressor load.
parts.engineering: Starting is a transient energy balance between starter and turbine torque, compressor work, drag, and rotor inertia. Insufficient airflow or excessive fuel can cause a hung or hot start, so starter speed and exhaust temperature are closely monitored.
parts.material: Steel and aluminium housing with pneumatic turbine or electric motor internals

parts.name: Engine-Driven Fuel Pump
parts.function: The pump supplies pressurised fuel for combustion and for hydromechanical actuation functions.
parts.howItWorks: A gearbox-driven pumping element raises fuel pressure above the level required by the metering unit and nozzle circuits. The electronic controller commands metering hardware to set actual engine fuel flow. Excess flow may be recirculated depending on system architecture.
parts.engineering: Pump displacement follows accessory speed while fuel demand follows the control schedule, so regulation and bypass provisions are needed across the operating range. High pressure supports atomisation and actuator response but increases leakage and heating concerns.
parts.material: Steel pumping elements in an aluminium housing with fuel-compatible seals

specs.label: Drive
specs.value: Mechanical drive from the accessory gearbox

parts.name: Oil Tank, Pump, and Filter Module
parts.function: This grouped lubrication module stores oil and routes it through engine bearings and gears.
parts.howItWorks: A pressure pump delivers filtered oil to bearing chambers and the accessory gearbox. Scavenge passages return used oil for de-aeration, cooling, filtration, and reuse. Sealing air helps keep the oil inside sumps despite rotating shafts and changing pressure.
parts.engineering: Lubrication carries away both friction heat and part of the bearing chamber's environmental heat. Filter differential pressure, chip detection, oil temperature, and scavenge flow provide early evidence of mechanical distress.
parts.material: Aluminium tank and pump bodies with steel gears and synthetic turbine oil

specs.label: Function
specs.value: Pressure lubrication, cooling, scavenging, and filtration

parts.name: Full-Authority Digital Engine Controller
parts.function: The redundant electronic controller schedules fuel and engine geometry to provide commanded thrust safely.
parts.howItWorks: It reads shaft speeds, pressures, temperatures, and aircraft commands, then calculates fuel and actuator commands. Control laws manage starting, acceleration, deceleration, idle, and limits without requiring the pilot to set each device manually. Redundant channels and fail-safe logic protect against sensor or electronics faults.
parts.engineering: The controller protects limits such as turbine temperature, spool speed, and compressor surge margin while minimising thrust response delay. Software, sensor voting, actuator feedback, and power-supply independence are central to safety and dispatch reliability.
parts.material: Aluminium electronics chassis with sealed connectors and circuit boards

specs.label: Control architecture
specs.value: Digital, typically multi-channel and fault tolerant

specs.label: Representative controlled outputs
specs.value: Fuel flow, variable vanes, and bleed valves

parts.name: Engine Wiring Harness
parts.function: Armoured cable runs carry sensor data, control commands, and electrical power around the engine.
parts.howItWorks: Branched harnesses connect the controller to valves, igniters, pumps, and instrumentation. Clamps hold the cables away from hot cases and vibrating edges, while sealed connectors resist fuel and oil. Shielding and separation reduce electromagnetic interference.
parts.engineering: Harness routing is constrained by vibration, heat, maintenance access, and electromagnetic compatibility. Small changes in clamp spacing can change chafing life, and redundancy requires separated routes so one local event cannot disable every control channel.
parts.material: High-temperature insulated conductors in braided and polymer protective sleeves

parts.name: Engine Fuel Supply Lines
parts.function: Rigid and flexible fuel lines connect the pump and metering hardware to the combustor manifold.
parts.howItWorks: The tubing follows the exterior of the core to remain accessible while avoiding extremely hot zones. Fittings and supported bends carry pressure pulses and vibration without excessive movement. Insulation or heat shields protect fuel from temperatures that promote coking.
parts.engineering: Tube routing needs enough compliance for thermal expansion without creating fatigue-prone motion at fittings. Leakage is both a fire hazard and a thrust-control problem, so support spacing, drainage, and inspection access are important.
parts.material: Stainless steel tube with high-temperature flexible sections and fittings

parts.name: Compressor Bleed and Anti-Ice Duct
parts.function: This duct transports hot compressed air for inlet anti-icing and other pneumatic services.
parts.howItWorks: Air is extracted from a suitable compressor port and routed around the core toward the inlet and accessory systems. Using an intermediate port reduces the energy penalty compared with taking all air from the final stage. Valves determine when the service receives flow.
parts.engineering: Every kilogram bled before the turbine reduces available core work and can reduce efficiency. The duct must tolerate pressure, vibration, and several hundred degrees of temperature while its expansion joints and supports avoid imposing excessive loads on case bosses.
parts.material: Thin-wall stainless steel or nickel-alloy duct with bellows and flanges

parts.name: Speed, Pressure, and Temperature Sensors
parts.function: Engine sensors supply the measurements needed for thrust control, health monitoring, and limit protection.
parts.howItWorks: Speed probes detect passing shaft features, pressure taps sample the gas path, and temperature probes measure critical turbine conditions. Their signals travel through the harness to the controller. Multiple sensing locations help distinguish normal changes from local faults.
parts.engineering: Turbine temperature probes face erosion and drift, while pressure lines can trap contamination or condensate. Control accuracy depends on calibration and dynamic response as well as nominal sensor precision, especially during rapid acceleration.
parts.material: Stainless steel and nickel-alloy probes with ceramic-insulated electrical elements

systems.name: Bypass Airflow
systems.explanation: Most fan air passes around the core rather than entering combustion. The outlet vanes remove swirl and the aft duct and nozzle convert the fan pressure rise into a large, relatively low-speed propulsive jet.

systems.name: Core Air and Hot-Gas Path
systems.explanation: The smaller core stream is compressed, diffused, mixed with fuel, burned, and expanded through the turbines. Turbines extract mechanical power before residual exhaust energy leaves through the core nozzle.

systems.name: Metered Fuel Path
systems.explanation: The gearbox-driven pump pressurises fuel, the controller commands the metered quantity, and the manifold distributes it to nozzles whose sprays mix with swirling compressor air.

systems.name: Low-Spool Mechanical Power
systems.explanation: The low-pressure turbine generates torque, the long inner shaft carries it forward, and the fan disk delivers it to the blades. The booster rotors share this low-pressure spool.

systems.name: Sensing and Control Commands
systems.explanation: Measurements feed redundant control computations. The resulting commands fan out to fuel metering and compressor actuators; the linear path is a simplified representation of several simultaneous branches.

steps.title: Open the nacelle
steps.narration: Remove the outer aerodynamic panels and inlet treatment first. They streamline and quiet the engine, but the heavy fan containment structure and all turbomachinery remain underneath.

steps.title: Disconnect external services
steps.narration: Trace the wiring, fuel, bleed-air, and oil hardware around the lower and outer core. The accessory gearbox mechanically links these services to the high-pressure rotor.

steps.title: Expose the fan
steps.narration: Lift away the containment ring to reveal the wide-chord fan. Notice that its blade tips sweep an area far larger than the core inlet.

steps.title: Remove the fan rotor
steps.narration: The spinner, blades, disk, and forward bearing come away as the fan module is dismantled. The long inner shaft and the stationary bypass vanes are now visible.

steps.title: Cross the bypass structure
steps.narration: Remove the outlet vanes and intermediate case. Their struts carry structural and service loads, yet leave most of the bypass annulus open for airflow.

steps.title: Open the compression system
steps.narration: The compressor case, stationary vanes, and bleed hardware expose the two compressor spools. Rotor and stator rows alternate, and blade height falls toward the combustor.

steps.title: Withdraw the compressor rotors
steps.narration: Pull the booster and high-pressure rotor assemblies off their concentric shafts. This reveals how the independent low- and high-speed mechanical systems occupy the same axis.

steps.title: Open the combustor
steps.narration: Remove the diffuser, fuel distribution hardware, igniters, and pressure case. The annular liner and first turbine nozzle now show where combustion ends and turbine expansion begins.

steps.title: Strip the hot section and exhaust
steps.narration: The case, shrouds, turbine rows, rear frame, and exhaust pieces come away from the hot end. Compare the compact high-pressure turbine with the larger multi-stage fan-driving turbine.

steps.title: Remove the final core elements
steps.narration: The combustor liner and low-pressure shaft are the last major represented elements. Review their relationship: combustion supplies gas energy, while two shafts return turbine work to the compressors and fan.

study.overview: A high-bypass turbofan is best understood as a gas generator driving an enormous fan. Air first passes the fan: most goes straight around the core and leaves as a large, relatively quiet bypass jet, while a smaller stream enters the core. Booster and high-pressure compressor rows squeeze that core air, and a diffuser slows it before fuel is sprayed into the annular combustor. Continuous burning raises the gas's energy, after which turbine nozzle vanes aim it at turbine blades. The compact high-pressure turbine drives the high-pressure compressor through the outer hollow shaft. The larger low-pressure turbine drives the front fan through the inner shaft. Remaining hot gas exits the core nozzle and adds thrust. A digital controller measures speed, pressure, and temperature, then schedules fuel, bleed valves, and variable vanes so the engine accelerates safely without overheating or compressor surge.

keyConcepts.title: Large airflow, modest jet speed
keyConcepts.body: At a given thrust, accelerating a large airflow by a smaller amount generally wastes less kinetic energy than accelerating a small airflow very rapidly. The high-bypass fan therefore produces most takeoff and cruise thrust, while the smaller core supplies power and an additional hot jet.

keyConcepts.title: Compression happens in many small steps
keyConcepts.body: Each rotor adds swirl and total energy; each stator turns and diffuses the flow. A single stage has limited stable pressure rise, so many stages are stacked and their flow areas shrink as density rises.

keyConcepts.title: The turbines are power take-offs
keyConcepts.body: Combustion does not push directly on the fan. The turbines convert hot-gas energy into shaft work, leaving only residual exhaust energy for the core jet. High- and low-pressure turbines are sized for different mechanical loads.

keyConcepts.title: Two spools improve matching
keyConcepts.body: The fan and its turbine turn on one shaft while the high-pressure compressor and turbine turn faster on another. Letting the spools choose different speeds keeps blade incidence and efficiency more acceptable from idle to takeoff.

keyConcepts.title: Surge is a system instability
keyConcepts.body: If compressor blades stall severely and downstream pressure remains high, airflow can break down or reverse. Variable vanes, bleed valves, careful acceleration fuel schedules, and clean blades preserve surge margin.

keyConcepts.title: Hot-section cooling is part of performance
keyConcepts.body: Compressor air cools turbine vanes, blades, liners, and shrouds. It consumes energy that was expensive to compress, so engineers trade cooling flow and component life directly against fuel efficiency.

keyConcepts.title: Clearance is both efficiency and safety
keyConcepts.body: Small blade-tip gaps reduce leakage, but rotating and stationary parts expand at different rates. Case cooling, abradable seals, and transient modelling seek small cruise clearances without rotor-to-case contact.

principles.title: Thrust and propulsive efficiency
principles.body: Ignoring installation drag, F = mdot core (V core - V0) + mdot bypass (V bypass - V0) + pressure-thrust terms. Ideal propulsive efficiency for a single jet is eta p = 2 V0 / (Vj + V0). High-bypass designs lower Vj for a given average momentum change, improving eta p but increasing fan diameter and nacelle drag.

principles.title: Euler turbomachinery work
principles.body: Specific rotor work is delta h0 = U2 V theta2 - U1 V theta1, where U = omega r. Blade speed and change in tangential velocity determine work input or extraction. For nearly adiabatic flow, delta h0 = cp delta T0, linking blade geometry directly to total-temperature change.

principles.title: Compressor pressure rise
principles.body: For an ideal compression process, T02 / T01 = PR raised to ((gamma - 1) / gamma). With isentropic compressor efficiency eta c, the real relation is T02 / T01 = 1 + [PR raised to ((gamma - 1) / gamma) - 1] / eta c. Required compressor work is approximately mdot cp (T02 - T01).

principles.title: Ideal gas-turbine cycle
principles.body: The simple ideal Brayton-cycle thermal efficiency is eta = 1 - PR raised to (-(gamma - 1) / gamma). Real engines depart through compressor and turbine inefficiency, pressure losses, cooling bleed, high turbine inlet temperature, and variable gas properties. Higher pressure ratio is useful only when component efficiency and turbine temperature capability support it.

principles.title: Shaft power and torque balance
principles.body: For each spool in steady operation, turbine power approximately equals compressor or fan power plus losses and accessory extraction. P = T omega and turbine P = mdot gas cp delta T0 turbine. During acceleration, net power increases spool kinetic energy according to net torque = I alpha.

quiz.question: What does the large fan at the front mainly do?
options: It decorates the nose
It pushes air backwards to help push the engine forwards
It stores fuel
It cools the pilots
quiz.explanation: The spinning fan gives a very large amount of air a rearward push. The reaction to that push creates most of the engine's thrust.

quiz.question: Where does the engine get the energy to spin its machinery?
options: From burning fuel with air
From paint on the fan blades
From the oil tank alone
From the shape of the outer cover
quiz.explanation: Burning fuel releases heat into compressed air. The turbines capture part of that hot gas's energy and use it to spin the compressors and fan.

quiz.question: Which statement correctly describes most air leaving the fan?
options: It all passes through the fuel nozzles
It passes around the core through the bypass duct
It is stored in the nacelle
It enters the oil system
quiz.explanation: In a high-bypass engine, most fan air goes around the combustor through the bypass duct and produces thrust directly. Only the smaller core stream enters compression and combustion.

quiz.question: Why can the high-pressure compressor spin faster than the large front fan?
options: They are connected by separate concentric shafts and turbines
The fan is not attached to any shaft
The fuel manifold changes their gear ratio continuously
The fan is stationary during cruise
quiz.explanation: The inner low-pressure shaft connects the fan to its turbine, while the outer hollow shaft connects the high-pressure compressor to its own turbine. Their speeds are linked by airflow but not rigidly locked together.

quiz.question: What is the main purpose of high-pressure turbine nozzle guide vanes?
options: Pump lubricating oil
Open the cowl for maintenance
Accelerate and aim hot gas into the turbine rotor
Remove swirl from bypass air before the fan
quiz.explanation: The nozzles turn pressure into directed high-speed flow at the angle needed by the following high-pressure turbine rotor.

quiz.question: Why is excessive compressor blade-tip clearance undesirable even if it prevents rubbing?
options: It increases leakage over the blades and wastes compression work
It always increases fuel pressure
It prevents the fan from producing bypass air
It makes the oil too cold
quiz.explanation: Leaking flow can bypass the intended blade passage without receiving the same work and pressure rise. Clearance control therefore balances efficiency against rub risk during thermal transients.

quiz.question: Why would the controller open compressor bleed valves during starting even though bleeding air wastes energy?
options: To improve stage matching and preserve surge margin
To increase the fan disk diameter
To heat the fuel tank
To lock both spools together
quiz.explanation: At low speed the compressor stages can be poorly matched to downstream pressure. Controlled bleeding unloads selected stages and helps avoid flow breakdown until the engine reaches a better operating condition.

quiz.question: If the low-pressure turbine must deliver more fan power without a proportional speed change, which quantities best summarise the additional demand?
options: Higher torque and greater gas total-temperature drop
Lower turbine work and lower fuel flow
Only a larger oil volume
Only a larger acoustic-liner area
quiz.explanation: Power is torque times angular speed, and turbine power comes mainly from gas mass flow times heat capacity times total-temperature drop. More fan power therefore needs more transmitted torque and generally more turbine energy extraction.
